title: Expressions
preamble:
# Expressions

The expression language used throughout
DS — `where` clauses, action-argument values, `emit` / `publish`
slot values, `cache` value, and every other position the
grammar lists `expression`. One grammar, one type system, one
set of built-in functions.

Paired with:
- [LGRA] for the expression-production
  syntax and precedence layering.
- [LFAC] and
  [LLOG] for how expressions
  interact with fact lifecycle and truth maintenance.
- Series-aggregation call syntax: this doc covers how
  aggregations compose as atoms in expressions;
  [LSER] owns the list of aggregation names
  and their semantics.

## What this is not

- Not a grammar reference for where expressions appear —
  [LGRA] owns that.
- Not a compiler-implementation guide. Lowering to the
  runtime's expression atoms is briefly noted at the end;
  detailed lowering lives with the runtime docs.
- Not a general-purpose numerical library. The built-in math
  set covers Python's `math` module minus esoterica. Things
  intentionally left out of the built-in set (compute them adapter-side if needed): `isnan` /
  `isinf` / `isfinite`, `gcd` / `lcm`, `factorial`,
  `copysign` / `fmod`, `erf` / `gamma` / `lgamma`,
  `frexp` / `ldexp`.
